cells.nuance: Trinitarian: one God in three persons, in Nicene Christianity.
No general dietary restriction across most branches.
A solar calendar, with some movable feasts set by rule.
From sacramental priesthood under bishops to congregational ministry, the range is the branch map itself.
Evangelism is mandated in most branches and central to the tradition's history.

cells.label: Created by God
cells.nuance: Creation from nothing by God; branches divide over literal readings of Genesis.
Clerical and monastic dress aside, lay codes are rare outside particular communities.
Love of God and neighbor as the law's summary, elaborated through virtue and conscience traditions.

cells.label: Grace through Christ
cells.nuance: Salvation through Christ; the branches' defining disputes concern faith, works, and sacraments.

cells.label: Bible; authority varies
cells.nuance: Scripture read with tradition and magisterium in Catholic and Orthodox Christianity, or as sole authority in Protestant principle.
Positions run from exclusivist to inclusivist; Nostra Aetate reset the Catholic stance in 1965.
Sunday worship, eucharistic or preaching-centered by branch, over a liturgical year.
